finding.claim: The icon URL supplied to update() is stored without validation and later fetched server-side with a GET in sync(). This is blind SSRF: the attacker can make the nightly job send requests to internal hosts or cloud metadata endpoints, but cannot read the response.
finding.source: update(String webhook, String icon) parameter icon at src/Profile.java:11, documented as PUT /profile (the HTTP handler is not in the repo, so the caller is inferred from the comment).
finding.sink: URI.create(iconUrl) and c.send(HttpRequest...GET()...) at src/Profile.java:23-24, run by the nightly sync() job.

trace.note: Only webhook is validated by regex; icon is not checked
this.iconUrl = icon stores the value unchanged
HttpClient sends the GET from the server; body is read and discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: No host, scheme, IP-range, or private-address validation on icon. Line 12 validates only webhook (fixed host hooks.example.com, 20 alphanumerics), so it is not SSRF. JDK HttpRequest restricts schemes to http/https (from JDK behaviour, not repo code). The HttpClient is passed in, so its redirect policy is unknown and may allow redirect-based reach.

verdict.guard_found: none: icon is stored unchanged at src/Profile.java:16 and used at :23 with no host, scheme, or address check; the only check is the webhook regex at :12.
verdict.reason: The trace misdescribes src/Profile.java:24, which uses BodyHandlers.ofByteArray() and so keeps the response body rather than discarding it (the discarding handler is at :22, for the webhook request), and the attacker control of icon rests on a PUT /profile handler that is not in the repo, so the finding as written does not hold, though the missing icon validation at :16 would likely still be a real issue if the caller is confirmed.
